title: 一番街入口・推定のカラー立体スタディ

coordinate_system.dimensions_status: Visual assumptions from oblique photographs and modern footprint context; not measured historical dimensions.
coordinate_system.authored_height_method: Each authored placement uses local source TIN height plus relative height; baseline context and shared route cameras remain absolute local Y.

scope.role: Near-field entrance corner and material/lighting look development. Outside the first 20 m, simple restrained context only.
scope.modern_context: Read-only layout-feature geometry is retained in a separate collection. Context within the entrance study envelope is hidden to avoid superimposing incompatible2025 and inferred period volumes.

references.source_date_status: Toyo Keizai photo archive caption attributes the matching wide daylight composition to1978, Junji Yoshino; exact day and negative record not recovered. The local filename night is misleading.
references.source_creator: 吉野純治 / Junji Yoshino, as attributed by Toyo Keizai
references.use: Entrance massing contrast; narrow pale tiled left facade, tall finned right corner, large separate analog sign cabinets, three-dimensional awnings, long sidewall with repeated structural bays. Colour target only: warm ivory tile, neutral concrete, vermilion paint, cobalt blue enamel, blue daylight. The rooftop Honjin board repeats the source-readable name in an inferred placement; it does not claim an exact rooftop advertisement.

references.source_date_status: Photograph label; museum ID7378 remains a comparison candidate
references.use: Material/depth lessons from deep left-front shop glazing, distinct structural mullions and lantern fittings; straight gate as explicitly dated optional study. The1972/1978 left facades are not proven to be the same structure. Warm lamps and tile surface relief are inferred from approved colour reference.

none.meaning: No gate hypothesis selected; absence in this render is not evidence of historical absence.

curved.geometry: Adopted post-centre span 10.25 m, outer base span 10.59 m, 6.5 m posts, 6.45 m oval centre and 7.8 m outer tail tips; all dimensions are explicit assumptions, parameters read from the adopted gate decision.

straight.geometry: Inferred horizontal gate; pole positions, rear and dimensions unresolved.

gate.adoption_status: Curved incandescent gate selected by reasoned inference under user authorization; 1978 evidence is extrapolated to the 1976 scene, not verified historical proof.

frontages.features: Pale tile piers, different floor-specific window divisions, restaurant sign panels, ground-floor glass recessed behind columns, striped canvas awning, sidewall glazing and shop interiors.
frontages.historic_identity_status: Readable suzuya sign source-based; facade dimensions and1976 configuration inferred.

frontages.features: Exposed vertical concrete fins, separate upper glazing, deep dark ground-floor portal, narrow individual lightboxes, blue pub fascia, curved metal service trim, open sidewall window bays.
frontages.historic_identity_status: Likely Komatsu building; owner interview dates eight-floor replacement to1973. Photographic match/dimensions, signs retained in1976 and unseen interior remain inferred.

rooftop_billboard.placement_status: adopted inference; not a copied historical rooftop programme

frontages.features: Darker terracotta concrete facade with continuous horizontal glazing and separate deep enamel bands.
frontages.historic_identity_status: Peripheral composition proxy; no verified business identity assigned.

frontages.features: Pale concrete bank-like frontage with individual window openings; excludes movie titles/programmes and human poster art.
frontages.historic_identity_status: Peripheral composition proxy; no verified 1976 frontage assigned.

sign_text.reading_status: straight gate header; optional variant only

materials.authored: Node-based PBR materials and modeled surface relief; no photograph textures or external mesh assets.
materials.palette: Ivory glazed tile and grout; aged off-white painted concrete; pale grey concrete fins; muted russet tile; vermilion painted steel; cobalt enamel; dark bronze window frames; smoky blue-grey glazing; dry fine aggregate asphalt.
materials.light: Blue-sky daylight with soft sun and restrained 2400 K incandescent appearance; AgX Medium High Contrast, exposure -0.8. Exact weather and time are authored.
materials.unseen_details: Interior bars, shades, shelves, drain covers, rooftop rails, service wiring, fixings and weathering are restrained period-compatible inventions. They do not establish a historical shop layout. Window air-conditioner cabinets, pane colour variation, rain traces and rooftop steel supports are inferred period-compatible details.
materials.colour_management: Authored palette is sRGB and converted to scene-linear for shader inputs.

cameras.entrance-approach: Shared proposal position, look target and 35 mm lens preserved; eye follows source TIN plus 1.6 m.
cameras.under-gate: Shared proposal position, look target and 35 mm lens preserved; eye follows source TIN plus 1.6 m.
cameras.entrance-calibration: Separate reference-framing camera: 48 m south of the gate, 1.6 m above source terrain, 24 mm lens and upward aim at relative height 14 m, showing both full facades and adopted rooftop signs.
cameras.near-facade: Separate oblique1.6 m detail camera inside the first 20 m; for depth and material inspection only.
cameras.entrance-gate-study: Separate closer composition: 17.8 m south, 1.6 m above terrain, 30 mm lens, upward target 6.1 m. This does not replace an existing route camera.

limitations: This is an adopted 1976 reconstruction with inferred dimensions and colours; visual completion does not establish historical certainty.
Curved incandescent gate is adopted using the 1978 photograph and the association history; the conflicting 1972 straight-gate evidence remains recorded in the decision.
Building widths/heights, source-camera positions, interiors, rear elevations and street fittings are not survey measurements.

The 1972 and 1978 left-front facades differ; the older photograph is used for depth/material lessons only. Exact shared building/entrance coordinates remain unresolved, including the reported earlier relocation of Suzuya.
The modern PLATEAU blockout is a placement reference; it is not evidence of 1976 buildings.
Uncertain small sign text and all cinema programmes/poster art are omitted. No generated raster is used as facade geometry or lettering.
No people, vehicles or crowd motion are included. They require separately sourced period assets and motion validation.
Visual QA and independent historical/visual critique must be recorded after Blender renders; script creation alone is not a passed visual round.
